uncited: Latent Space Representation methods map input images to a compact, structured latent code (tokens, features, or distributions) which is subsequently decoded into explicit 3D Gaussian primitives, enabling generalizable reconstruction without per-scene optimization [16746-feed-forward-generalizable-reconstruction.md].

Unlike sibling methods that predict Gaussians directly from pixel-wise features or cost volumes, this family explicitly models the scene as a set of learnable latent entities (e.g., tokens or entropy-coded features) to enforce global consistency, reduce representation bloat, or handle ambiguity [16746-feed-forward-generalizable-reconstruction.md].

All methods in this family share the core objective of mapping input image features to a set of 3D Gaussian parameters $\mathcal{G} = \{\mu, \Sigma, \alpha, c\}$ without per-scene gradient descent [16746-feed-forward-generalizable-reconstruction.md].
**Input Representation:** Inputs are typically one or more RGB images $I \in \mathbb{R}^{H \times W \times 3}$ [16746-feed-forward-generalizable-reconstruction.md].

Some methods require known camera poses $P$, while others (e.g., [Splatt3R](16423-splatt3r.md), [ZeroGS](16425-zerogs.md)) predict poses or operate on uncalibrated inputs [16746-feed-forward-generalizable-reconstruction.md].
**Feature Encoding:** A shared encoder (e.g., Vision Transformer, CNN) extracts multi-scale features from the input images [16746-feed-forward-generalizable-reconstruction.md].
Cross-attention or cost volumes are often used to aggregate multi-view information [16746-feed-forward-generalizable-reconstruction.md].
**Primitive Prediction:** A decoder head predicts Gaussian attributes [16746-feed-forward-generalizable-reconstruction.md].
* **Color ($c$):** Spherical Harmonics (SH) coefficients or constant RGB [16746-feed-forward-generalizable-reconstruction.md].

**Differentiable Rendering:** The predicted Gaussians are rendered into target views using differentiable rasterization to compute reconstruction losses (e.g., L1, SSIM, LPIPS) for training the network [16746-feed-forward-generalizable-reconstruction.md].

**Generalization:** The network is trained on a large dataset of scenes to learn priors about geometry and appearance, allowing inference on unseen scenes [16746-feed-forward-generalizable-reconstruction.md].

By decoupling feature aggregation from primitive instantiation via a latent space, methods like GlobalSplat and latentSplat address the "representation bloat" and local consistency issues of direct pixel-wise regression [16571-globalsplat.md, 18652-latentsplat.md].
CodecSplat extends this by addressing the storage and transmission inefficiencies of irregular Gaussian primitives [18143-codecsplat.md].
